newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Berlusconi renews offer to Prodi on EMU.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Berlusconi renews offer to Prodi on EMU.

text.p: Opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi has renewed an offer to work with Italy's governing coalition on measures to help the country be in on the start of Europe's single currency in 1999.

Newspapers reported on Saturday that Berlusconi told Prime Minister Romano Prodi in a meeting late on Friday that the centre-right oppositon was willing to support his government in its drive to qualify for economic and monetary union (EMU).

The government, which recently rammed a huge 62.5 trillion lire ($37 billion) deficit-cutting budget through parliament, is preparing further cuts of 13 to 15 trillion lire to the deficit in the form of an additional mini-budget.

But the Marxist party Communist Refoundation, which ensures the centre-left government's majority in parliament, has raised questions over whether fresh budgetary pain was worth the cost and cast doubt over the prospects of EMU.
Berlusconi, a media magnate and former prime minister, said his offer contained no ulterior motives.
"We don't want to upset the government's majority," Berlusconi was quoted as saying in most newspapers.
"But perhaps now the government, helped by our availability on this point, will be able to work with Communist Refoundation from a position of strength," he said.
Berlusconi first made his offer to Prodi last week, when he proposed working with the government on an early 1998 budget in return for a combined assault on Italy's costly welfare system.

Communist Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti, who has said his party would vote against any measures containing cuts to welfare, urged the government to "refuse the offer from Berlusconi, who is seeking to break up the majority".
Prodi said he was optimistic after meeting Berlusconi.
"I nurture high hopes for the opposition's new attitude on issues regarding Europe," Prodi said. "The head of the opposition wants to give a hand to the government," he added.
But he said he was confidant the ruling coalition would find support for the mini-budget from its parliamentary majority, including Communist Refoundation.
"We're sure the majority will recognise itself in a unified proposal that we shall present in parliament," Prodi said.
"We will go into parliament with our majority, but this time we will expect a sense of responsibility which the opposition has promised -- an availability to vote without any preconceptions.
"I believe, I hope, that this is possible," he concluded.
